title: Meeting American expatriates: Coleman, Nicholas, Mezzrow, Bishop, Waters
summary: In Europe he saw Bill Coleman, Albert Nicholas, Mezz Mezzrow, Walter Bishop and Benny Waters, old friends who had settled abroad.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Right, well were you jamming with French musicians, or were they some --
Yes, uh-huh.
Americans that were over there? Did you run into any Americans?
Yes, I did. Coleman! I saw Coleman.
Coleman?
I saw Coleman -- Bill Coleman.
Oh, Bill Coleman.
Bill Coleman, yeah, and I saw the clarinet player that died not just too long ago, I'm talking about --
Albert Nicholas?
Albert Nicholas, yeah.
Albert Nicholas, right.
And he was there. Uh, (unintelligible). Mezz Mezzrow!
(Laughter.)
Mezz hasn't changed a bit!
(Unintelligible). Man! How you think --
good to see you! Man! He's the same -- he was the same cat.
(Laughter.)
His son -- his son played the drums.

But I didn't meet him -- I didn't see him then, because last time I saw him -- his son, he must have been about 12 or 13. I saw him on 126th Street, here in New York, you know, because
I was living at 126th Street, and they used to -- they lived down the street from me, and I'd see him past, and I would -- his mother Mezz.
Who the heck else. Bish -- Bishop.
Walter Bishop?
Walter Bishop. He came by, he came by to see us, and --
He's a -- the one -- the musicians you're talking about now are those who had settled over there, who were living over there.

Yeah, they were living over there. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. I missed seeing the tenor man. I'll call his name, that used to work with me when I was with Charlie Johnson. Heck of a man, too. I called his name the first time. (Unintelligible.)
Oh, Howard Johnson? No, he was an alto.
No, no, I would play -- was on the alto then. Benny Waters.
Oh, Benny Waters. Right. Right.
